title: Your Big Brain Wouldn’t Be Possible Without Sugar
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEvolutionYour Big Brain Wouldn’t Be Possible Without SugarPass the glucoseJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on August 6, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHumans have big brains, and those brains come with a big appetite for energy. The focus on what fueled the evolution of our massive noggins has centered on protein from meat, but a new analytical review published today in Science is reframing the story around a much sweeter center: glucose.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured Video“While animal foods were important, the brain’s need for glucose has largely received little attention from anthropologists,” study author Jennie Brand-Miller said in a statement.Nutritional scientists from the University of Sydney and University of Glasgow modeled dietary intake versus energy needs for varying brain and body sizes across 4 million years of hominin evolution. The models relied on data from the dietary composition of primates, fossil dental isotopes and morphology, genetics, and more. Over this 4-million-year period, brain size of hominins quintupled from 300 grams in Australopithecus afarensis to 1,500 grams in modern Homo sapiens, and metabolic needs increased accordingly.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
